# M0 fixtures

`calibration-1920x1080.png` is an original synthetic 1920×1080 calibration scene with a 120-pixel grid, road corridor and lane marks. It contains no external media. Use it to check fit, 100%, zoom-to-pointer and pan. `corrupt.png` intentionally contains invalid bytes.

Run `python scripts/generate_fixtures.py` to regenerate fixtures and original application icons using Python's standard library. Rust tests generate their own Unicode source files, EXIF orientation-6 JPEG, changed/missing sources, oversized file and temporary SQLite projects. No user images are modified during testing.

## M2 video fixtures

`video/cfr.mp4`, `vfr.mp4` and `rotated.mp4` are original synthetic H.264 clips generated by `python scripts/generate-video-fixtures.py` with FFmpeg 9.0.2. They contain 12/13 presentation-order frames, B frames, variable PTS spacing and a verified display rotation of 90 degrees. No third-party footage is included. `expected.json` records hashes and independent FFprobe PTS output; the Rust acceptance test asserts actual rotation metadata, not merely a filename.

`npm run test:m2:acceptance` generates a separate project and compares extracted pixels with a complete sequential decode, checks manual/interval selection, cancellation, duplicate identity, grouped splits, COCO RLE and YOLO parser acceptance. Parser source/dependencies live only in ignored `.cache`, fetched explicitly by the documented preparation commands. Standard unit tests generate their own polygon-with-hole, disconnected-component, uncompressed/compressed RLE, schema-2 backup and corrupt-cache fixtures.
